vars.title: Log level
vars.tooltip: Verbosity of sing-box logs

vars.name: certificate_store
vars.title: Certificate store
vars.tooltip: Root certificates used to verify TLS servers. On Android 7.x and older the system store is outdated — Let's Encrypt and other modern authorities are missing, so TLS nodes fail to connect. Switch to Mozilla or Chrome to use an up-to-date bundle shipped inside the app.

vars.name: auto_detect_interface
vars.title: Auto-detect interface
vars.tooltip: Automatically detect the default network interface

vars.name: direct_connect_timeout
vars.title: Direct connect timeout
vars.tooltip: How long the core waits for a direct TCP connect before giving up. sing-box default is 5s; mobile networks that lose SYN packets need more. Android itself retries for about 2 minutes, apps usually wait 10-30s. Format: 15s, 1m, 1m30s.

sections.name: Internal
sections.description: Internal globals referenced by presets — not shown as VPN settings.

vars.name: resolve_enabled
vars.title: Resolve destination IP
vars.tooltip: Resolve the sniffed domain to an IP before routing, so GeoIP and IP rules can match. Turn off when using FakeIP — the fake IP already carries the domain, and a real lookup here would bypass FakeIP and can fail on a broken resolver.

vars.name: resolve_strategy
vars.title: Resolve strategy
vars.tooltip: IP version preference for DNS resolution

vars.name: urltest_url
vars.title: Test URL
vars.tooltip: Endpoint for measuring proxy latency. Pick a preset or type any URL — 204 / tiny-body endpoints are best.

vars.name: urltest_interval
vars.title: Test interval
vars.tooltip: How often sing-box re-tests and re-picks. Lower → faster switching, but more background traffic and battery: each cycle dials the servers (waking suspended tunnels). 15m is the battery-friendly default.

vars.name: urltest_tolerance
vars.title: Tolerance (ms)
vars.tooltip: Only switch proxy if latency difference exceeds this

vars.name: dns_strategy
vars.title: Preferred IP version
vars.tooltip: DNS resolution strategy

vars.name: dns_default_domain_resolver
vars.title: Default domain resolver
vars.tooltip:
Used by routing engine to resolve hostnames internally (outbound endpoints, routing rules). Not the resolver apps use.

  • dns_shield — default; races 6 encrypted providers over a direct connection, answers from whichever replies first
  • google_doh, cloudflare_dot — recommended; encrypted, direct

⚠ Plain UDP servers go through the tunnel and can't answer before it is up — don't use them here.
⚠ local_dns_resolver here leaks lookups to your ISP — system DNS bypasses the VPN.

vars.name: dns_final
vars.title: DNS final
vars.tooltip:
Default fallback DNS server. Used when an app's DNS query doesn't match any DNS rule.

  • dns_shield — default; races 6 encrypted providers over a direct connection, answers from whichever replies first
  • google_doh, cloudflare_dot — recommended; encrypted, direct
  • cloudflare_udp, google_udp — plain UDP through the tunnel; fine here

local_dns_resolver (system DNS) is safe here.

vars.name: dns_cache_capacity
vars.title: DNS cache size
vars.tooltip: Number of cached answers (1024..65535).

vars.name: dns_optimistic
vars.title: Serve stale answers
vars.tooltip: Answer from cache at once and refresh in the background.

vars.name: dns_resolver_no_stale
vars.title: Never serve stale answers for node hostnames
vars.tooltip: Hostnames the core resolves itself (node servers) are looked up again once the cached answer expires, so a node whose address changed does not stay on the old one. App DNS queries are not affected.

vars.name: dns_store_cache
vars.title: Keep DNS cache after restart
vars.tooltip: Store the DNS cache in cache.db so it survives a restart.

vars.name: tun_address
vars.title: IPv4 address
vars.tooltip: TUN interface address (CIDR)

vars.name: ipv6_enabled
vars.title: Enable IPv6
vars.tooltip: Add an IPv6 address to the tunnel. Off by default — turn on only if your network has working IPv6. Turning on sets resolution to prefer IPv4, turning off forces IPv4-only — you can change the strategy in DNS Settings.

vars.name: tun_address6
vars.title: IPv6 address
vars.tooltip: TUN interface IPv6 address (CIDR). Applied only when Enable IPv6 is on.

vars.name: route_address_enable
vars.title: Split default route
vars.tooltip: Send all traffic to the tunnel as two half-ranges per address family instead of one default route. The same traffic goes through the tunnel; turn on only if the device ignores the VPN's default route.

vars.name: tun_route_exclude
vars.title: Bypass the tunnel
vars.tooltip: Addresses (CIDR) that skip the tunnel and the core entirely, e.g. a home NAS. Their traffic goes without VPN: routing rules, DNS hijack and statistics do not see it. Do not add networks you reach through a VPN node, the FakeIP pool or the tunnel's own address. Applies after a full VPN restart.

vars.name: tun_name
vars.title: TUN interface
vars.tooltip: system name

vars.name: tun_mtu
vars.title: MTU
vars.tooltip: 9000 recommended (sing-box default)

vars.name: tun_auto_route
vars.title: Auto route
vars.tooltip: Let sing-box manage routing table

vars.name: tun_strict_route
vars.title: Strict route
vars.tooltip: May break connectivity on some devices

vars.name: tun_stack
vars.title: Stack
vars.tooltip: system (default), gvisor (userspace), mixed

sections.name: VPN Mode
sections.description: Local proxy inbound vars (hidden — values come from VpnModeConfig)

vars.name: vpn_mode
vars.title: VPN mode
vars.tooltip: How the core captures traffic. Set from VPN Settings → Mode.

options.title: Proxy — local port only, no TUN

vars.name: proxy_type
vars.title: Local proxy protocol
vars.tooltip: Inbound type for the local proxy port.

options.title: Mixed — HTTP + SOCKS5 on one port

vars.name: proxy_listen
vars.title: Listen address
vars.tooltip: IPv4 the local proxy binds to. Suggestions above; any valid IPv4 is allowed (e.g. a specific LAN IP). Anything other than 127.x is reachable from the network and forces auth on.

vars.name: proxy_port
vars.title: Listen port
vars.tooltip: Local proxy port (1024..65535).

vars.name: proxy_user
vars.title: Proxy username
vars.tooltip: Username for proxy auth (when auth is on).

vars.name: proxy_pass
vars.title: Proxy password
vars.tooltip: Password for proxy auth. Auto-generated when auth turns on.

vars.name: proxy_auth
vars.title: Require auth
vars.tooltip: Whether the local proxy requires username/password. Forced on for non-loopback listen.

vars.name: sys_proxy
vars.title: System HTTP proxy
vars.tooltip: Announce a local HTTP proxy to the VPN network (Android 10+).

vars.name: sys_proxy_port
vars.title: System proxy port
vars.tooltip: Loopback port of the system HTTP proxy inbound.

sections.name: TLS Fragmentation
sections.description: Splits the TLS handshake so it carries no single-packet signature. Default for all servers; override per server, folder or subscription.

vars.name: tls_fragment
vars.title: TLS Fragment
vars.tooltip: Split TLS ClientHello into small TCP segments

vars.name: tls_record_fragment
vars.title: TLS Record Fragment
vars.tooltip: Split handshake into multiple TLS records (try this first)

vars.name: tls_fragment_fallback_delay
vars.title: Fallback delay
vars.tooltip: Wait time when automatic detection fails

vars.name: tls_mixed_case_sni
vars.title: Mixed-case SNI
vars.tooltip: Randomize letter case in server_name (WwW.gOoGle.CoM). Per RFC 6066 the field is case-insensitive, so servers accept either form; defeats naive exact-match matching only. Skipped on REALITY nodes — their SNI must stay byte-exact

ui.label: Traffic Processing
ui.description: Core packet handling: sniff the domain, hijack DNS into the tunnel, resolve destinations for routing. Applied first, before all other rules.

vars.name: sniff_enabled
vars.title: Packet sniffing
vars.tooltip:
Detect protocol and domain from packets for accurate routing.
⚠️ WARNING: turning this off stops protocol matching (e.g. BitTorrent, TLS, QUIC), and domain matching too unless FakeIP is on.

vars.name: sniff_timeout
vars.title: Sniff timeout
vars.tooltip: How long to wait for the domain to appear in the packet before giving up.

vars.name: hijack_dns_enabled
vars.title: Hijack DNS
vars.tooltip:
Route all DNS queries through the tunnel's DNS engine.
⚠️ WARNING: turning this off disables FakeIP and all DNS rules — apps query their own DNS directly, uncontrolled. Keep on unless you know exactly why.

ui.label: Block Ads
ui.description: Reject ad-related connections. Downloads rule set (~1 MB).

ui.label: Ru internet segment
ui.description: Route Russian TLDs (.ru/.su/IDN), service CDNs (Yandex/VK/Avito/2GIS/banks/etc), Russian IP ranges and Russian apps (by package name) directly.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to route traffic for Russian domains and IPs

vars.name: dns_enable
vars.title: DNS
vars.tooltip: Send matched domains to this preset's DNS server and apply DNS-level options like Force IPv4. Turn off to keep routing without DNS changes.

vars.name: dns_ip
vars.title: UDP server IP
vars.tooltip: The IP sets the Yandex DNS profile: Base, Safe or Family. Off: this server is not used.

vars.name: dns_dot_ip
vars.title: DoT server IP
vars.tooltip: The IP sets the Yandex DNS profile: Base, Safe or Family. Off: this server is not used.

vars.name: dns_doh_ip
vars.title: DoH server IP
vars.tooltip: The IP sets the Yandex DNS profile: Base, Safe or Family. Off: this server is not used.

vars.name: dns_encrypted_via_outbound
vars.title: Encrypted DNS via Outbound
vars.tooltip: Send Yandex DoT and DoH through this preset's Outbound, like UDP. Off: they go direct.

vars.name: geoip_enabled
vars.title: GeoIP IP-range fallback
vars.tooltip: Match Russian-AS IPs as well as domains — catches CDN/QUIC/ECH cases where domain detection fails. Auto-downloads geoip-ru.srs (~150 KB) on first use.

vars.name: apps_enabled
vars.title: Russian apps by package
vars.tooltip: Route Android apps from the legiz-ru list (banks, marketplaces, government services, Yandex/VK and others) by package name, regardless of the domains they use. Auto-downloads ru-app-list.srs (~4 KB) on first use.

vars.name: force_ipv4
vars.title: Force IPv4
vars.tooltip: Resolve Russian domains to IPv4 only. Prevents dead IPv6 connections on networks without working global IPv6. Works through this preset's DNS rule — keep the DNS toggle on. Turn off if your network has functional IPv6.

ui.label: FakeIP
ui.description: Instant DNS via placeholder IPs; real names resolve inside the tunnel. Speeds up DNS and prevents pre-tunnel DNS leaks. Not a DPI bypass. Enable below special domains so GeoIP direct routing still works.

vars.name: dns_enable
vars.title: DNS
vars.tooltip: Apply this preset's FakeIP DNS handling. Turn off to disable FakeIP without removing the preset.

vars.name: dns_server
vars.title: FakeIP server
vars.tooltip: The FakeIP allocator. Internal — bound to the fakeip DNS server.

vars.name: force
vars.title: Block HTTPS records
vars.tooltip: Reply empty to HTTPS/SVCB DNS records (RFC 9460) so apps fall back to plain A/AAAA. Keeps these queries from leaking to the fallback DNS.

vars.name: inet4_range
vars.title: IPv4 pool
vars.tooltip: Fake IPv4 addresses are taken from this range (CIDR). Change it if the default range is used in your network or excluded from the tunnel. Changing it resets the saved fake addresses.

vars.name: inet6_range
vars.title: IPv6 pool
vars.tooltip: Fake IPv6 addresses are taken from this range (CIDR). Leave empty to answer AAAA queries with no address. At least one pool must be set.

ui.label: Russia-only services
ui.description: Services available only inside Russia. Direct by default, or route via a direction to reach them from abroad.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to route Russia-only services. Direct on a Russian network; pick a Russian direction to reach them from abroad.

vars.name: force_ipv4
vars.title: Force IPv4
vars.tooltip: Resolve these domains to IPv4 only. Prevents dead IPv6 connections on networks without working global IPv6. Turn off if your network has functional IPv6.

ui.label: BitTorrent
ui.description: Route BitTorrent traffic. Direct by default, or send it to a separate direction.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to route BitTorrent. Direct to keep it off the VPN, or pick a direction to tunnel it.

ui.label: Tunnel ingress
ui.description: Connections arriving from a client tunnel (WireGuard, AWG, OpenVPN, OpenConnect) are rejected unless the node's own switches allow them: access to this device, the local network, or using this device as a gateway. The settings below choose what happens to the rest and where allowed and gateway traffic goes.

vars.name: closed_out
vars.title: Incoming from tunnels
vars.tooltip: What happens to connections arriving from a tunnel that the node's switches did not allow. reject (default) and drop close them; an outbound forwards them.

vars.name: allowed_out
vars.title: Device and local network go to
vars.tooltip: Outbound for peers allowed to reach this device or the local network.

vars.name: gateway_out
vars.title: Gateway traffic goes to
vars.tooltip: Outbound for peers allowed to use this device as a gateway.

ui.label: Tailscale networks
ui.description: Route each tailnet through its Tailscale node and resolve its names with the node's own DNS.

vars.name: dns_enable
vars.title: DNS
vars.tooltip: Resolve tailnet names with the node's own DNS.

ui.label: Private IPs
ui.description: Route private IP ranges (LAN). Direct by default, or send to a direction to reach routers/devices over a local VPN.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to route private/LAN IPs. Direct for local access, or a direction to reach a remote LAN over VPN.

ui.label: Unknown traffic
ui.description: Traffic in the tunnel not attributed to any installed app (background/foreign processes) goes direct, bypassing the VPN, so a process that binds to the tunnel cannot learn the server address. Pick Reject to drop it instead.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: outbound
vars.tooltip: Direct = send it outside the VPN. Or pick Reject to drop it (strict mode: any attribution failure means no network).

ui.label: VoWiFi (carrier calling)
ui.description: Keep Wi-Fi Calling off the VPN. Phones reach the carrier's IMS gateway (ePDG) under the 3GPP service domain, and an IKEv2/IPsec tunnel carries the calls. Routed through a VPN the voice picks up delay and jitter, and the carrier sees the IMS registration coming from a foreign address. Direct keeps calls on the home network.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to send VoWiFi traffic. Direct keeps it off the VPN — that is the point of this preset.

vars.name: ike_ports
vars.title: Match IKE ports (500/4500)
vars.tooltip: Also route UDP 500/4500 directly. Some modems get the gateway address from the carrier network and never send a DNS query, so the domain rule alone misses them. Those ports carry nothing but IPsec key exchange.

ui.label: Google push (FCM)
ui.description: Send only Google push traffic (FCM ports 5228-5230 and FCM hosts) outside the VPN, so notifications arrive on time with the screen off. Does not touch the rest of Google Play, so your Play region stays intact. If your DNS goes through the tunnel, add a matching direct rule in DNS settings — otherwise the hosts resolve to the wrong region and push stays silent.

vars.name: outbound
vars.title: Outbound
vars.tooltip: Where to send push traffic. Direct keeps it off the VPN — that is the point of this preset.

vars.name: gms_only
vars.title: Limit to Google Play Services
vars.tooltip: Match only traffic from com.google.android.gms instead of any app. Narrower, but app matching works in VPN mode only — leave off if you use proxy mode.
